meta.title: Risk Register — every decision path
meta.scoring: Likelihood and Impact are each scored 1 (Very Low) to 5 (Very High). Score = Likelihood x Impact, 1 to 25. Bands: 1-4 Low, 5-9 Moderate, 10-14 Elevated, 15-19 High, 20-25 Severe.
meta.honesty_rule: Where a likelihood is anchored in an official published statistic, the anchor is named in the 'basis' field and the row is marked OFFICIAL. Where no official statistic exists, the row is marked JUDGEMENT and is also listed on the Flagged for Review page. No judgement-based likelihood is presented anywhere on this site as a verified number.
meta.black_swan_definition: A black-swan row is one where a low-probability event produces damage disproportionate to the asset's income, and where the loss is not diversifiable within a single-asset, single-tenant position.

official_anchors.anchor: 30-year probability of an M6.7+ earthquake in the Los Angeles region = 60% (UCERF3)
official_anchors.derived: Probability within any five-year window = 1 - 0.40^(5/30) = 14.2% compound, or 60% x 5/30 = 10.0% linear

official_anchors.anchor: JACK on Track block closure programme = approximately 150-200 underperforming restaurants, against a fiscal-2025 opening system of 2,191
official_anchors.derived: 6.8% to 9.1% of the system is scheduled for closure over the programme
official_anchors.s: Jack in the Box Inc., Form 10-K and Form 10-Q filed with the SEC

official_anchors.anchor: Company-disclosed ongoing annual closure rate = 1% of system units, with fiscal 2025 at 1.5% to 2.0%
official_anchors.derived: Cumulative probability that any given restaurant closes within n years at 1% per year = 1 - 0.99^n. Four years (to 2030) = 3.9%. Nine years (to 2035) = 8.6%.
official_anchors.s: Jack in the Box Inc. plan as disclosed in SEC-filed materials

official_anchors.anchor: January 2025 Eaton and Palisades fires cost $5.2 billion to $10.1 billion in economic output; Los Angeles County 2024 GDP was $818.5 billion
official_anchors.derived: A January-2025-class fire event removed between 0.64% and 1.23% of one year of county economic output
official_anchors.s: County of Los Angeles official fact sheet; U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis

official_anchors.anchor: Measure ULA = 4% or 5.5% of the entire consideration or value; County documentary transfer tax and City documentary transfer tax also apply
official_anchors.derived: A City of Los Angeles sale at or above the ULA threshold carries transaction tax of roughly 4.5% to 6.1% of gross price before brokerage and legal costs
official_anchors.s: City of Los Angeles Housing Department official ULA FAQ; LA Municipal Code Section 21.9.2

official_anchors.anchor: Proposition 13: base rate 1% of assessed value; assessed value may rise at most 2% a year absent a change in ownership; a change in ownership establishes a new base-year value at full market value
official_anchors.derived: A sale converts a tax bill that may be far below market into one at approximately 1% of price plus direct charges, which the buyer prices into the offer and which the NNN tenant must reimburse
official_anchors.s: California State Board of Equalization; Los Angeles County Assessor

official_anchors.anchor: FHFA All-Transactions HPI, Los Angeles-Long Beach-Glendale MSAD: +1.2% year over year to 2026 Q2; FHFA purchase-only Pacific division: 0.0% year over year in 2026 Q1
official_anchors.derived: Local real-asset price growth is at or below national inflation of +3.6% (BLS LA CPI-U), i.e. real price decline
official_anchors.s: FHFA via the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics

official_anchors.anchor: U.S. Treasury par yield curve, November 5, 2026: 10-year 4.84%, 30-year 5.25%, 2-year 4.46%
official_anchors.derived: The official risk-free anchor is high and the curve is positively sloped; no official series supports assuming near-term cap-rate compression

risks.risk: Tenant does not renew at the 2030-2035 expiry because the restaurant is selected for closure under the JACK on Track programme
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — ANC-2 and ANC-3: 6.8%-9.1% of the system is scheduled for closure and the company states closures follow franchise agreement termination dates. The score reflects programme-level exposure, not a site-specific probability, because no site-level list exists (T-43).
risks.mitigant: Option B step 3: obtain the franchise agreement expiration date and a written statement of renewal intent years before expiry. Pre-commit the sell trigger.

risks.risk: Tenant insolvency or rent interruption before expiry, driven by negative transaction trends, falling average unit volumes and rising franchisee bad debt
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — T-03, T-08, T-09, T-26: system same-store sales -1.1% in fiscal 2026 Q3 driven by transaction decline; franchise AUV down 3.8% in fiscal 2025; franchisor reports higher franchisee bad-debt expense.
risks.mitigant: Confirm counterparty identity and guaranty (A-12, A-13). Track late payments monthly as a sell trigger. A corporate head lease with a franchisee sub-lease (T-25) materially reduces this risk versus a bare franchisee lease.

risks.risk: Earthquake of magnitude 6.7 or greater damaging or destroying the improvements
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — ANC-1: USGS UCERF3 30-year probability 60% for M6.7+, 46% for M7.0+, 31% for M7.5+, equivalent to 10.0% (linear) or 14.2% (compound) inside a five-year window. Likelihood band 2 reflects the five-year decision window, not the 30-year figure.
risks.mitigant: Confirm seismic code vintage and retrofit status (H-40); confirm Alquist-Priolo zone status, which also creates a statutory disclosure duty on sale (H-05, H-38); verify earthquake coverage and limits — a standard commercial property policy excludes earth movement.

risks.risk: Wildfire damaging the improvements or shutting down the trade area, and a resulting regional economic contraction
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — ANC-4: the January 2025 Eaton and Palisades fires destroyed 16,251 structures, killed 31 people, impacted about 6,800 businesses and 47,000 workers, and cost $5.2-10.1 billion in county economic output (0.64%-1.23% of one year of county GDP). Direct-fire likelihood for a central-LA commercial parcel is lower than for interface housing, but the City's Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone includes Hollywood, Silver Lake, Echo Park, Los Feliz, Mount Washington and El Sereno.
risks.mitigant: Run the LACoFD Fire Hazard Severity Zone lookup for the parcel (H-37). If the parcel is inside a VHFHSZ, confirm Chapter 7A construction compliance, defensible space and insurance availability before choosing to hold. Track California Department of Insurance FAIR Plan commercial policy counts as a leading indicator (H-28).

risks.risk: Flooding of the parcel or of the trade area, including riverine flood
risks.basis: JUDGEMENT for the likelihood band. The parcel-level FEMA determination is blank (H-36) and the FEMA National Risk Index county values could not be read from fema.gov in this session (H-31 to H-34). What IS official: FEMA is the publisher of the flood map and the National Risk Index, and the Central City North plan area is bounded on the east by the Los Angeles River (G-03).
risks.mitigant: Complete the FEMA Flood Map Service Center determination for the parcel (H-36). Confirm whether the tenant's NNN insurance obligation includes flood cover, which is excluded from standard commercial property policies.

risks.risk: Measure ULA imposes 4% or 5.5% of the ENTIRE sale price if the parcel is inside the City of Los Angeles and at or above the indexed threshold
risks.basis: OFFICIAL for the mechanism — R-09, R-10, R-11, R-15 (LAHD official FAQ and LAMC Section 21.9.2). The CURRENT INDEXED THRESHOLDS are UNVERIFIED (R-12) and flagged. Likelihood band 3 because applicability turns on two facts not yet established: whether the parcel is in the City, and where the price sits relative to the threshold.
risks.mitigant: Establish jurisdiction first (R-15). Verify current thresholds in writing with the City Office of Finance. Model the cliff explicitly: because the tax applies to the whole price, a price just above the threshold can net LESS than the threshold itself, creating a dead band where a higher price reduces proceeds.

risks.risk: Proposition 13 reassessment on sale reduces the price a buyer will pay
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — ANC-6, R-02, R-04: a change in ownership establishes a new base-year value at full market value, and V-22 shows the county applied the maximum 2% factor in 2026 because California CPI exceeded the cap. If the owner has held the asset for many years the gap between assessed value and market value is large.
risks.mitigant: Pull the current assessed value from the Assessor (A-10) and quantify the buyer's post-sale tax step-up. A long-held, low-assessed asset should be marketed on the strength of its in-place tax position, and the step-up priced into expectations rather than discovered in negotiation.

risks.risk: Reinvestment risk: proceeds must be redeployed into a 4.84% ten-year Treasury environment with no official evidence of cap-rate compression and a flat Pacific-division real-asset market
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — ANC-7 and ANC-8: FHFA LA MSAD +1.2% year over year; FHFA Pacific division 0.0% year over year in 2026 Q1; BLS LA CPI-U +3.6%; 10-year UST 4.84%. Real (inflation-adjusted) local asset prices are flat to declining.
risks.mitigant: Do not sell without a named reinvestment destination. If Option F is used, confirm statutory exchange deadlines before listing.

risks.risk: Selling into competing supply: the franchisor is itself a net seller of restaurant real estate
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — T-13: fiscal 2026 Q3 other operating income of $3.1 million was 'primarily due to an increase in gains on the sale of real estate'; T-35: the JACK on Track plan includes selling a select number of owned real estate holdings; T-34: the company still holds $93.3 million of owned land.
risks.mitigant: Time the listing to precede, not follow, a company real-estate disposal programme announcement. Differentiate on trade-area fundamentals (household growth, Metro access) rather than on brand.

risks.risk: Capital gain, depreciation recapture and state tax crystallise on sale
risks.basis: JUDGEMENT for the impact band. The mechanism is certain; the magnitude is unknowable here because basis, holding period and entity structure are personal financial information withheld under the privacy protocol (A-17, R-23).
risks.mitigant: Obtain a professional tax determination before listing. Evaluate Option F (Section 1031 exchange) as a deferral, subject to verified statutory deadlines.

risks.risk: Alquist-Priolo disclosure duty arises on sale if the parcel is inside an Earthquake Fault Zone
risks.basis: OFFICIAL for the duty — H-05: PRC Section 2621.9 requires a seller to disclose to the buyer that the property lies within an earthquake fault zone. Parcel status is blank (H-38). H-06 shows CGS released proposed NEW and REVISED zones for Los Angeles County, so the map is expanding.
risks.mitigant: Run the CGS zone lookup before marketing. An undisclosed zone is a post-closing liability; a disclosed one is a pricing item.

risks.risk: Firm term decays every year held, mechanically reducing the eventual sale price of the income stream
risks.basis: OFFICIAL as to mechanism. Net-lease value is a function of remaining firm term; this is arithmetic, not forecast. What is NOT verifiable is the magnitude, because no official cap rate exists (V-28).
risks.mitigant: This is the central argument against Option C. Option B neutralises it by lengthening firm term instead of consuming it.

risks.risk: Rent escalation fails to keep pace with cost inflation, compressing tenant margins and raising closure probability
risks.basis: OFFICIAL for the inputs — I-11 LA CPI-U +3.6%; I-17 food +3.5%; I-18 energy +18.0%; I-20/I-21 City minimum wage +3.08% to $18.42; T-39 84% of restaurant employees part-time; R-20 the company itself cited California payroll taxes in its margin discussion. The lease escalator is unknown (A-07).
risks.mitigant: Establish the escalator (A-07). A fixed-escalator lease in a 3.6%-inflation market transfers real income away from the landlord; a CPI-linked lease transfers it to the tenant's cost base and raises closure risk. Both are adverse — they are adverse in different ways.

risks.risk: Trade-area demand erodes from continued population loss and tightening federal migration policy
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — D-03 city population -0.8% 2020-2025; D-06 county -3.2%; D-12 county -64,000 in 2025; D-13 city -0.9% in 2025-26; D-08 California -0.14% and -54,000, its first annual loss after three years of gains; D-09 net legal international migration halved to 126,400; D-18 the city is 35.7% foreign-born.
risks.mitigant: Weigh against D-32/D-33/D-36: SCAG projects city households +21.5% and city jobs +8.5% by 2035, and county households +6% by 2050 even with population -5%. Household formation, not population, is the correct demand driver for a drive-thru site.

risks.risk: Daytime office population in central Los Angeles continues to contract
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — E-20 Information sector employment -5.7% year over year (September 2026 preliminary), the weakest supersector in the region; E-19 Financial Activities -1.7%; E-18 Manufacturing -1.2%; E-17 Professional and Business Services -0.5%; E-11 total nonfarm only +0.5%.
risks.mitigant: Offset by E-15 Education and Health Services +3.8% and E-13 Leisure and Hospitality +1.5%, and by G-06 Metro D Line Section 1 opening May 8, 2026 along Wilshire Boulevard.

risks.risk: Property tax and direct charges rise on renewal or on a reassessment event, and under NNN the tenant must reimburse them
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — R-01 base rate 1%; R-02 2% cap; R-03 the maximum 2% factor was applied in 2026 because California CPI exceeded the limit; V-22 that factor added about $43 billion to the county roll. S-19 notes local school bond measures appear as direct charges and are parcel-specific.
risks.mitigant: Confirm the Tax Rate Area and total rate (R-05). A 2% annual step in the tenant's tax reimbursement, on top of a $18.42 minimum wage and 3.6% food inflation, is a cumulative affordability problem for a franchisee whose average unit volume already fell 3.8%.

risks.risk: Extended downtime after expiry with the landlord carrying tax, insurance and maintenance previously paid by the tenant
risks.basis: JUDGEMENT. No official source quantifies QSR re-tenanting downtime. The mechanism is certain: on expiry of an NNN lease all three cost lines revert to the landlord (R-06, R-01).
risks.mitigant: Begin alternative-operator outreach at least 24 months before expiry. Confirm zoning and use permits in advance (G-22).

risks.risk: Second-generation conversion capital required (demolition, kitchen infrastructure, drive-thru reconfiguration, signage) with no verified cost basis
risks.basis: JUDGEMENT — no official source. Conversion cost is private market data. Flagged rather than estimated.
risks.mitigant: Obtain contractor pricing before electing Option D. Do not elect Option D on the strength of this report alone.

risks.risk: Entitlement risk: zoning, General Plan land use and overlay designation are unknown, and the Downtown Community Plan update is still in process
risks.basis: OFFICIAL as to the planning framework — G-01, G-02, G-03, G-04: the Downtown Community Plan consolidates Central City and Central City North and guides development through 2040; the Central City plan in effect was adopted in 2003 and an update is underway. Parcel-specific zoning is blank (G-22).
risks.mitigant: Confirm zoning and plan designation before committing capital. The 2040 plan horizon extends beyond the lease expiry, so entitlement value cannot be crystallised inside the decision window without an adopted plan.

risks.risk: The existing NNN lease may contain exclusive-use, continuous-operation or landlord-termination restrictions that block redevelopment
risks.basis: JUDGEMENT for the likelihood. The lease was not supplied (A-03), so no clause can be verified. Continuous-operation and exclusive-use covenants are standard in QSR leases but their presence here is unknown and is not asserted.
risks.mitigant: Read the lease. Do not model any redevelopment value until the covenant package is confirmed.

risks.risk: Counterparty commitment obtained from interim management proves unreliable
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — T-15: Mark King is identified in the company's own SEC-filed release as INTERIM Chief Executive Officer. T-16: the company completed the sale of Del Taco on December 22, 2025 and is now single-brand. T-33: fiscal 2025 restructuring, integration and strategic initiative charges of $7,298 thousand.
risks.mitigant: Any extension must be documented by the corporate entity, not by a regional operator, and must survive a change of control. Verify execution authority.

risks.risk: Insurance cost or availability deteriorates for a commercial property in a re-mapped fire hazard zone
risks.basis: OFFICIAL and FAVOURABLE at present — H-26, H-27, H-28, H-29: the California Department of Insurance reported on May 1, 2026 that FAIR Plan growth slowed to about 16,000 residential policies in Q1 2026 from 35,000-50,000 per quarter in 2024 through September 2025, that COMMERCIAL policies were stable at 21,200 rising to 21,464, and that nine top-ten insurers committed to expanding coverage. H-07: LA County Local Responsibility Area Fire Hazard Severity Zones were re-established in 2025, so a parcel can newly fall inside a designated zone.
risks.mitigant: Re-run the FHSZ lookup after each CAL FIRE mapping cycle. Under NNN the tenant carries the insurance, but an uninsurable site produces tenant default and then landlord exposure.

risks.risk: Local economic contraction from a large-scale federal immigration-enforcement shock
risks.basis: OFFICIAL — D-08, D-09, D-12: the California Department of Finance attributes the state's first annual population loss in four years to federal policy changes that cut net legal international migration by more than half, from 248,400 in 2024 to 126,400 in 2025, and lists 'deportations' as one of three causes of Los Angeles County's 64,000-person 2025 loss. The city is 35.7% foreign-born (D-18) and the county 33.4%.
risks.mitigant: Monitor the Department of Finance E-1 release each May. A demand base that is unusually exposed to migration policy is a structural, not cyclical, feature of this trade area and should be priced into any hold decision.

risks.risk: Brand-level obsolescence: the Jack in the Box concept loses relevance to the trade area's demographic profile
risks.basis: OFFICIAL as to direction — T-03: fiscal 2026 Q3 sales declined 'primarily' on lower transactions; T-02: the company closed 17 restaurants and opened 4 in the quarter; T-20: the brand remains at least the fourth largest QSR hamburger chain in each of its top ten markets, which comprise about 70% of the system. Transaction-led decline across four consecutive reported periods is a demand-relevance signal, not a price signal.
risks.mitigant: Track transaction trends rather than sales trends in each quarterly filing. Price-led growth masks traffic loss; traffic-led decline does not.

risks.risk: Interest-rate environment: a higher risk-free rate suppresses net-lease pricing at exit
risks.basis: OFFICIAL for the level — ANC-8: 10-year UST 4.84%, 30-year 5.25%, 2-year 4.46% on November 5, 2026, a positively sloped curve with the 10s2s spread at +38 basis points. No official series supports assuming compression.
risks.mitigant: Model the exit across the cap-rate sensitivity grid on the Projection page rather than at a single assumed rate. Recognise that a 30-year hold competes with a 5.25% risk-free 30-year instrument.

risks.risk: Sale price lands in the Measure ULA dead band, where a higher gross price produces lower net proceeds
risks.basis: OFFICIAL for the mechanism — R-10: the LAHD FAQ records the tax as 4% OF THE CONSIDERATION OR VALUE, i.e. of the whole price. The thresholds themselves are unverified (R-12).
risks.mitigant: Once the current thresholds are verified in writing with the City Office of Finance, compute net proceeds at the threshold and just above it, and set a reserve accordingly.

risks.risk: Analysis paralysis: the four decisive facts (counterparty, option structure, jurisdiction, parcel hazards) remain unresolved and the decision window closes by default
risks.basis: OFFICIAL as to the gaps themselves — A-05, A-06, A-07, A-10, A-11, A-12, A-13, H-36, H-37, H-38, R-05, R-15 are all blank with official lookups linked. Every one of them is resolvable from public records or from documents the owner already holds.
risks.mitigant: This is why Option B step 1 has a three-month window and why the sell trigger in step 4 is pre-committed rather than negotiated in the moment.

risks.risk: Data-vintage risk: the official series underpinning this analysis are revised or discontinued
risks.basis: OFFICIAL and already realised — E-35: BEA has DISCONTINUED GDP and personal income statistics for metropolitan statistical areas, metropolitan divisions and combined statistical areas, so MSA-level GDP is no longer available. D-35 versus D-37: SCAG's 2025 draft reverses the direction of its own adopted 2024 forecast for LA County population. S-17: NCES CCD membership and CDE Census Day enrolment are different universes for the same district. E-38: Census QuickFacts publishes no business or employment fields at City of Los Angeles level.
risks.mitigant: Every row on this site carries its vintage and publisher. Re-verify before transacting. Four specific irregularities are logged on the Repo Audit & Irregularities page.
